name: schedules-timer-start
description: Stage 1 of #612: on boot the hub coordinator starts the schedules grid timer, and a schedule already due in ~/.kollab/schedules.json fires exactly once. The timer start is logged, the fire is recorded as a line in ~/.kollab/schedules-runs.jsonl, and the schedule is never deleted from schedules.json (Waiting rule). Scratch HOME, --no-daemon, no keyring.

setup.description: seed ~/.kollab/schedules.json with a schedule due two minutes ago

steps.description: the coordinator started the schedule timer
steps.command: for i in $(seq 1 25); do grep -rq "schedule timer started" "$HOME/.kollab/projects" 2>/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 1; done; echo 'no schedule-timer start line in the logs'; exit 1

steps.description: the due schedule fired and is recorded in the run log
steps.command: for i in $(seq 1 50); do [ -s "$HOME/.kollab/schedules-runs.jsonl" ] && exit 0; sleep 1; done; echo 'no run recorded in schedules-runs.jsonl'; exit 1

steps.description: the run record names the schedule and agent
the schedule is still stored (never deleted for firing)
